subject: Post-call: data handling statement & model improvement exclusion
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medsentry.health>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@medsentry.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: data controls and model-learning request

Hi Samir / Laura —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same page:  

- Customer ask: Medsentry requires no customer data to be used to improve or retrain Redwood production models.
- Residency: prefer provisioned region in US-East (us-east-1) for all workloads during pilot.
- Logs/PII: any logs that may contain PII should be minimized and purged within 30 days; backups should be scoped and clearly documented.
- Evidence: you requested a written confirmation and supporting docs (SOC2 summary and DPA/addendum).

Attached is a quick one-page controls summary we discussed (proposed-data-controls-summary.pdf). I’ll loop in legal and contracts to get a formal addendum in place — sharing Monica on that.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll send a formal written confirmation that Medsentry’s data won’t be used for model training and a draft DPA for signature.
2) Provide redacted SOC2 snapshot and logging/retention implementation notes.
3) Small mutual action plan and timeline for pilot (we aim for a 2-week DPA turnaround).

Do these steps and the 30-day retention target match your expectations? If yes, I’ll follow up with the draft documents by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0118 | diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medsentry.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medsentry.health>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: data controls and model-learning request

Thanks Diego — quick confirmation from our side:  

- Medsentry requires explicit, written confirmation that any customer-provided data (including prompts, responses, attachments, or logs) will NOT be used to train or fine-tune any of Redwood’s models or placed into training pipelines that could influence production model weights.
- For logs that must be retained for debugging, we require automatic purging of entries that may contain PII within 30 days.
- Residency for the pilot must be US-East (we will escalate if the region cannot be guaranteed).

We’re happy to review a draft DPA/addendum and SOC2 summary. As part of procurement, we’ll need DocuSign-ready language for the no-training clause and a short mutual action plan (dates + owners).

Laura — looped you since you’ll own legal review; happy to coordinate on next steps.

— Samir
Director, Platform Security | Medsentry Health
samir.gupta@medsentry.health

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medsentry.health>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@medsentry.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: data controls and model-learning request — formal statement and docs attached

Samir / Laura —

Appreciate the clarity. Per our conversation, attached are:  
- Redwood_DPA_Medsentry_draft.pdf (draft addendum with no-training clause highlighted)
- SOC2-Redwood-redacted.pdf (controls snapshot)
- proposed-data-controls-summary.pdf (one-pager from earlier)

Key points from the draft addendum (callouts):
1) No training on customer data: "Redwood Inference will not use Customer Data (including prompts, responses, file attachments, or derived artifacts) to train, fine-tune, or update production model weights or variants unless Customer provides explicit written consent."
2) Telemetry & debugging: we may retain aggregated, de-identified telemetry for system reliability; any PII-containing logs will be treated per the retention schedule below unless Customer objects in writing.
3) Retention: standard retention for operational logs is 30 days for entries that may contain PII; we will implement automated purging and will not include backups that contain PII beyond the stated retention window without Customer approval.
4) Residency: production inference and primary logs for the pilot will be hosted in US-East (us-east-1).

Action requested: please review the attached draft addendum. If language looks OK, we can route the DPA for signature via DocuSign (link included below). If you’d like a narrow edit (e.g., stricter retention or specific language on backups), Monica can pick up and propose contractable wording.

DocuSign preparation link: https://docusign.net/DocuSign/prepare?env=prod&documentId=abc123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/RDW-2027-MED-0243

I’ve also included Monica and Aditya to help with contract language and engineering controls.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Medsentry_draft.pdf (341KB, PDF), SOC2-Redwood-redacted.pdf (500KB, PDF)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medsentry.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@medsentry.health>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: data controls and model-learning request — formal statement and docs attached

Diego / Monica —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear draft. A couple of clarifications before we proceed to signatures:  

1) Backups: can you confirm whether operational backups are scheduled beyond the 30-day window and, if so, whether backups can be excluded from containing PII or whether they will be encrypted/sequestered and considered outside the purge window? We need to be explicit in the DPA about backups.
2) De-identified telemetry: we’re ok with aggregated metrics for reliability, but we’d like the addendum to expressly prohibit re-identification attempts and to require you to certify de-identification techniques in writing.

If you can incorporate the two bullets above into the DPA draft (or give us proposed contract language), we’ll route to legal immediately and aim to return a signed DPA within 72 hours. Otherwise, we’ll surface during legal review which may slow the timeline.

Thanks — I’ll circle back once our counsel reviews.

Laura Chen
Head of Procurement | Medsentry Health
laura.chen@medsentry.health
